title: Securities Trading Policy
date_next_review: At least once every two years (replaces the version dated 23 May 2023)

tiers.name: Team Members
tiers.description: All directors, officers and employees of The Lottery Corporation and its controlled entities, and all contractors, consultants, secondees and other personnel required to comply with its policies. Subject to the insider trading prohibition, company-imposed trading notices and, where they participate in an equity or incentive plan, the hedging and derivative ban over restricted and unvested awards; not subject to Blackout Periods or pre-clearance.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of The Lottery Corporation. Must obtain written pre-clearance from the Chairman (the Chairman applies to the Chairman of the Audit Committee) before Trading at any time, are barred from Trading in Blackout Periods, from Short Selling, Short-term Trading, margin lending and granting lenders any rights over their Securities, and must notify the Company Secretary of changes in notifiable interests within two business days.

tiers.name: Restricted Employees
tiers.description: Executives reporting directly to the MD & CEO (ELT members), Team Members reporting directly to ELT members, and any other Team Member determined by the Board, Chairman or MD & CEO to be a Restricted Employee. Same substantive restrictions as Directors, with pre-clearance from the Company Secretary or MD & CEO (ELT members: the Company Secretary, or the MD & CEO and the Chairman; the Company Secretary: the MD & CEO).

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: Any person or entity which might in the circumstances be reasonably associated with The Lottery Corporation or any of its Directors or Team Members, including spouses, partners, dependent children, family trusts, family companies, joint venture partners, and companies, trusts, partnerships and other entities (including self-managed superannuation funds) that such persons control or significantly influence. Directors and Restricted Employees must seek pre-clearance and make notifications on their Associates' behalf.

definitions.hedging_definition: A transaction that limits the economic risk of the exposure to the Securities acquired.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Continuous Disclosure Committee may, from time to time without prior notice, and conditionally or unconditionally, extend, reduce or create an additional Blackout Period. Separately the Board or Chairman may at their absolute discretion and without prior notice impose ad hoc restrictions, including a pre-clearance requirement, on some or all Team Members; and the company may notify Team Members not to Trade for a specified period or until further notice. No obligation to give reasons; a refusal or withdrawal of pre-clearance must be kept confidential by the applicant.

rules.detail: Plan participants and their Associates are banned from entering any derivative arrangement in respect of restricted shares and unvested performance options or rights. No venue limit and no approval route.
rules.evidence: Team Members participating in any of The Lottery Corporation's employee or executive equity or incentive plans and each of their Associates, are prohibited from: ... entering into a derivative arrangement in respect of restricted shares and unvested performance options or rights granted under these plans.

rules.detail: The ban expressly extends to 'restricted shares', that is shares that have vested or been allocated but remain subject to a disposal restriction, so shares still held under plan restrictions cannot be collared even though they are no longer unvested.
rules.evidence: prohibited from: hedging the value of restricted shares and unvested performance options or rights; and entering into a derivative arrangement in respect of restricted shares and unvested performance options or rights

rules.detail: Derivatives over vested, unrestricted shares are not prohibited. Securities expressly include over-the-counter options, equity swaps and hedges whether cash settled or not, and creating a hedge over Securities is covered Trading, so an OTC put or call requires written pre-clearance from the Chairman, must be executed within three business days and cannot be entered in a Blackout Period.
rules.evidence: any derivatives of those Securities, including equity swaps, contracts for difference, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options, whether settled by cash or otherwise

rules.detail: Same position as Directors, with pre-clearance from the Company Secretary or MD & CEO (ELT members: the Company Secretary, or the MD & CEO and the Chairman). Pre-clearance may be refused without reasons and may be refused for non-compliance with the applicable Minimum Shareholding Policy.
rules.evidence: A Director or Restricted Employee who wishes to Trade in The Lottery Corporation Securities at any time must obtain written pre-clearance

rules.detail: Hedging, defined as a transaction that limits the economic risk of the exposure to the Securities acquired, is banned over restricted shares and unvested performance options and rights for all plan participants and their Associates. A collar is squarely within that definition.
rules.evidence: prohibited from: hedging the value of restricted shares and unvested performance options or rights;

rules.section: Hedging and Derivatives; Pre-clearance to Trade
rules.detail: The hedging prohibition is confined by its terms to restricted shares and unvested awards, so hedging vested unrestricted shares is not prohibited. Creating a hedge over Securities is covered Trading, so it needs written pre-clearance from the Chairman, outside a Blackout Period, executed within three business days.
rules.evidence: creating a hedge, security interest, margin loan or other financial interest over or in relation to Securities;

rules.section: Hedging and Derivatives; Pre-clearance to Trade
rules.detail: As for Directors, with pre-clearance from the Company Secretary or the MD & CEO. The hedge is Trading, so the Minimum Shareholding Policy screen and the confidentiality of any refusal apply.
rules.evidence: Team Members participating in any of The Lottery Corporation's employee or executive equity or incentive plans and each of their Associates, are prohibited from: hedging the value of restricted shares and unvested performance options or rights

rules.section: Margin lending and other security interests
rules.detail: Monetisation is not named as such, but any monetisation that gives a financier recourse to the shares is caught by the flat ban on granting lenders any rights over the person's Securities. A purely unsecured cash-settled monetisation would instead be Trading requiring pre-clearance.
rules.evidence: Directors and Restricted Employees must not, and must ensure their Associates do not, enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any The Lottery Corporation Securities, or grant lenders any rights over their The Lottery Corporation Securities.

rules.detail: Flat ban on Directors, Restricted Employees and their Associates. Short Selling is defined narrowly as selling financial products with a view to repurchasing at a lower price, so a covered collar over shares actually held is not Short Selling on the policy's own definition.
rules.evidence: Directors and Restricted Employees must not, and must ensure their Associates do not, engage in: Short Selling (selling financial products with a view to repurchase the shares at a lower price) of The Lottery Corporation Securities;

rules.detail: The Short Selling ban is directed only at Directors, Restricted Employees and their Associates.

Securities lending is not named and is not listed in the description of covered Security Trading, although a stock loan to a lender would in practice offend the ban on granting lenders any rights over the person's Securities.

rules.section: Appendix 1 (Securities); Short Selling and Short-term Trading
rules.detail: Contracts for difference are expressly within the definition of Securities, so trading one is Trading requiring written pre-clearance outside Blackout Periods. In practice a CFD would be caught by the Short-term Trading ban (closing within six months of acquisition) and, if taken short, by the Short Selling ban.
rules.evidence: any derivatives of those Securities, including equity swaps, contracts for difference, futures, hedges and exchange-traded or over-the-counter options

rules.section: Key Principles; Margin lending and other security interests
rules.detail: Directors, Restricted Employees and their Associates are prohibited from margin lending. The first limb is confined to a margin loan or similar funding arrangement entered into to acquire Securities; the second limb, granting lenders any rights over their Securities, is unconfined and captures a facility secured on shares already held.
rules.evidence: Restricted Employees, Directors and their Associates are prohibited from engaging in Short Selling, Short-term Trading, margin lending, and from granting any rights over their The Lottery Corporation Securities.

rules.detail: The margin lending and security interest prohibitions bind only Directors, Restricted Employees and their Associates.

rules.section: Margin lending and other security interests
rules.detail: Granting a lender any rights over The Lottery Corporation Securities is prohibited outright for Directors, Restricted Employees and their Associates, with no vesting-state limit, no threshold, no approval route and no exemption. Creating a security interest over Securities is separately identified as covered Trading.
rules.evidence: or grant lenders any rights over their The Lottery Corporation Securities.

rules.section: What Trades in Securities are covered by this Policy
rules.detail: For Team Members who are not Directors or Restricted Employees, creating a security interest over Securities is covered Trading but no pre-clearance or prohibition attaches to it; only the insider trading prohibition and any ad hoc restriction apply.

rules.section: Key Principles; Margin lending and other security interests
rules.detail: The second limb of the margin lending clause is a general ban on secured financing: no rights of any kind may be granted to a lender over the person's Lottery Corporation Securities. This is the decisive obstacle to the loan leg of a funded collar and there is no discretion to waive it, the exceptional circumstances relief being limited to selling or disposing of Securities.
rules.evidence: Directors and Restricted Employees must not, and must ensure their Associates do not, ... grant lenders any rights over their The Lottery Corporation Securities.

rules.section: Short Selling and Short-term Trading; Exceptional circumstances
rules.detail: Short-term Trading, defined as Trading shares within six months of the acquisition, is banned for Directors, Restricted Employees and their Associates, except in exceptional circumstances where the Trading is the only reasonable course of action available and written pre-clearance is obtained.
rules.evidence: Short-term Trading (Trading within six months of the acquisition) of The Lottery Corporation Securities, except in exceptional circumstances where the Trading is the only reasonable course of action available and where written pre-clearance is sought and obtained in accordance with this Policy.

rules.detail: The Short-term Trading ban binds only Directors, Restricted Employees and their Associates.

financing.minimum_shareholding_requirement: Yes. The Policy is to be read with the Non-Executive Director Shareholding Policy and the Executive Shareholding Policy, and pre-clearance may be refused where the applicant is not, or as a result of the proposed Trading will not be, in compliance with the applicable Minimum Shareholding Policy. The policy does not say whether hedged or encumbered shares are excluded from the count.

exemption_authority: MD & CEO, or the Chairman in the case of Directors, may grant pre-clearance to sell or otherwise dispose of Securities during a Blackout Period or on a short-term basis in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship or a pressing financial commitment, court order, enforceable undertaking or other legal or regulatory requirement) where the Trading is the only reasonable course of action available. The relief runs to sales and disposals only; there is no power to waive the hedging, margin lending or security interest prohibitions.

bespoke_clauses.topic: grant of any rights to lenders
bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Restricted Employees must not, and must ensure their Associates do not, enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement to acquire any The Lottery Corporation Securities, or grant lenders any rights over their The Lottery Corporation Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The second limb is a flat ban on giving a financier any rights over the shares, which defeats the secured loan leg of a funded collar regardless of vesting state, loan purpose or loan-to-value ratio.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Employees, Directors and their Associates are prohibited from engaging in Short Selling, Short-term Trading, margin lending, and from granting any rights over their The Lottery Corporation Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Key Principles restate the ban without even the word 'lenders', so on the policy's own summary a written call option granted over the shares to the bank is at risk of being read as a prohibited grant of rights, not merely the security interest.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Security Trading covered by this Policy includes: ... creating a hedge, security interest, margin loan or other financial interest over or in relation to Securities;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Every element of a funded collar, the put, the call, the charge and the loan, is separately a Trade requiring written pre-clearance and falling outside Blackout Periods, so there is no argument that only the share sale is regulated.

bespoke_clauses.topic: restricted shares included in hedging ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: prohibited from: hedging the value of restricted shares and unvested performance options or rights; and entering into a derivative arrangement in respect of restricted shares and unvested performance options or rights granted under these plans.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Only shares that are both vested and free of plan restrictions can be collared, so the collar pool must be carefully identified against the plan records.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any Trading that is the subject of pre-clearance must be executed within three business days of the receipt of the written pre-clearance (unless the pre-clearance is withdrawn).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The whole structure would have to be priced, documented and executed inside three business days of clearance, and the clearance can be withdrawn in the meantime.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any pre-clearance to Trade can be given, withdrawn, refused or made subject to conditions by the applicable approver in their absolute discretion and without giving reasons. If pre-clearance is withdrawn or refused, the person seeking the pre-clearance must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The bank cannot rely on obtaining or keeping clearance, and the executive may be barred from explaining to the bank why a trade cannot proceed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: An application for pre-clearance to Trade in The Lottery Corporation Securities may be refused where the applicant is not, or as a result of the proposed Trading will not be, in compliance with the applicable Minimum Shareholding Policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even the derivative legs can be refused if the collar would leave the director or executive short of the minimum shareholding, so the collared parcel should sit above that requirement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Continuous Disclosure Committee may also, from time to time without prior notice, and conditionally or unconditionally, extend, reduce, or create an additional Blackout Period. ... The Board or Chairman may also, from time to time, at their absolute discretion, and without prior notice, impose ad hoc restrictions.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unannounced blackouts can block entry, roll, unwind or physical settlement at any time, and the executive bears that timing risk.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Short-term Trading (Trading within six months of the acquisition) of The Lottery Corporation Securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Collar tenor and any early unwind must sit beyond six months from the acquisition of the underlying shares, or fall within the narrow exceptional circumstances relief.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Associates means any person or entity which might in the circumstances be reasonably associated with The Lottery Corporation or any of its Directors or Team Members (such as spouses, partners, dependent children, family trusts, family companies, joint venture partners).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Holding the shares through a family trust, family company or self-managed superannuation fund does not escape the security interest ban or the pre-clearance regime.

summary: A funded collar is not possible for a Lottery Corporation Director or Restricted Employee. The derivative legs alone would be workable over vested, unrestricted shares: the hedging and derivatives ban is confined to restricted shares and unvested performance options and rights, Securities expressly include over-the-counter options, equity swaps and hedges whether cash settled or not, and creating a hedge is simply Trading that requires written pre-clearance from the Chairman (Directors) or the Company Secretary or MD & CEO (Restricted Employees), executed within three business days, outside the 1 January, 1 July and 1 October Blackout Periods and any additional blackout imposed by the Continuous Disclosure Committee. The loan leg fails: Directors and Restricted Employees and their Associates must not 'grant lenders any rights over their The Lottery Corporation Securities', an unqualified prohibition with no vesting-state limit, no threshold and no waiver power, and the Key Principles state it even more broadly as a ban on 'granting any rights over' their Securities. The exceptional circumstances discretion extends only to selling or disposing of Securities in hardship or under legal compulsion, so it cannot be used to authorise a secured facility. Any structure would therefore have to be unsecured and cash settled, sit beyond six months from acquisition to avoid the Short-term Trading ban, and leave the executive compliant with the applicable Minimum Shareholding Policy, since pre-clearance may be refused on that ground.
